findings.element: .undo strip (src/notes.js:1712) vs .carryStrip/undo pill (src/tasks.js:1330-1340, timer src/tasks.js:2348) vs .b-undo bar (src/timeline.js:1270-1300)
findings.problem: Same gesture class, same Ctrl Z, three different promises. Notes says 'Sent to Tasks. Undo Ctrl Z for 30 seconds' and TICKS the number down each second (UNDO_SECONDS = 30, src/notes.js:260). Tasks says '<Title> done' with no stop, no window, and retires the strip after 6000ms (src/tasks.js:2348) while its announcement only says 'Press Ctrl Z to undo.' Timeline says '<Title> moved 7 days earlier.' in a 1096x64 WHITE inline bar and never expires at all. Three grammars (bare adjective / verb-only / full sentence) and three truths about how long the way back lasts.
findings.fix: One window and one sentence shape. Hoist UNDO_SECONDS to one shared constant, set Tasks 6000 to the same value, and give all three the shape '<what happened>. Undo [Ctrl Z]' -- 'Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is done.', 'Sent to Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when.', 'Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days earlier.' Drop the ticking 'for N seconds' (it is the only moving number in the suite and it exists in one product only); if a window is worth stating, state it once in the same words everywhere.
